assumptions.value: sum by (user) (increase(cortex_query_fetched_chunk_bytes_total[10m]))

assumptions.name: rule queries
assumptions.value: included — rules are evaluated remotely, so every tenant's rule queries are in this pool alongside its user queries, and no label separates the two (inferred: the ruler's job (job=~".*ruler") evaluated rules but has no cortex_distributor_query_duration_seconds_count data, which a ruler evaluating locally always records, so its queries go to the query-frontend)

assumptions.value: 40.00 EUR per query-frontend-month × 1 = 40.00 EUR/month

assumptions.name: querier price

assumptions.name: driver
assumptions.value: cortex_prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds_sum (rule-evaluation seconds), total increase over 10m

assumptions.name: driver query
assumptions.value: sum by (user) (increase(cortex_prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds_sum[10m]))

assumptions.name: rule evaluation
assumptions.value: remote (inferred: the ruler's job (job=~".*ruler") evaluated rules but has no cortex_distributor_query_duration_seconds_count data, which a ruler evaluating locally always records, so its queries go to the query-frontend): the rule queries' work is priced in the query path

assumptions.name: price
assumptions.value: 60.00 EUR per ruler-month × 1 = 60.00 EUR/month

notes: rules are evaluated remotely, so this time is mostly the ruler waiting on the query path, not ruler CPU: it shows how long each tenant's rules occupy the ruler, and the work behind it is already in the query path pool. It also depends on load — a tenant's rules run slower when a neighbour loads the cluster

rules are evaluated remotely, so a tenant's rule queries drive its share of both the query path (the work) and the ruler (the time spent waiting for it). Each pool's cost is split once, so nothing is counted twice, but a rule-heavy tenant's total weighs the same queries in both

assumptions.name: output metric
assumptions.value: a recording rule's record: name is the metric it writes

assumptions.name: series count
assumptions.value: point-in-time, at 2026-10-22T03:26:59Z; not an average over the cost window, so shares divide it by a window average (see notes)
assumptions.source: Mimir query API, queried as each rule's own tenant

assumptions.name: count query
assumptions.value: count by (__name__) ({__name__=~"<name>|<name>|..."})
assumptions.source: Mimir query API, queried as each rule's own tenant

assumptions.name: count queries in pool 6
assumptions.value: the count queries run through the query path as each tenant, so they are recorded in that tenant's query-path (pool 6) counters, like any other API query. This run read pool 6 before counting; a later run whose window includes this one charges them to each tenant counted
assumptions.source: Mimir query API, queried as each rule's own tenant

assumptions.name: what is counted
assumptions.value: every series named after the rule's record: name in the tenant, including any written by something other than this rule

assumptions.name: presence
assumptions.value: an instant query counts series with a sample inside the lookback window (5m by default), which is close to, but not the same as, the ingester's active-series idle timeout

assumptions.name: denominator
assumptions.value: cortex_ingester_active_series (active series) per tenant, averaged over the 10m ending 2026-10-22T03:26:59Z, divided by the replication factor

assumptions.name: replication factor
assumptions.source: ingest storage: one owner per partition, zone replicas collapsed with max, so there is nothing to divide

notes: these counts are queries run as each tenant through the query path, so they appear in that tenant's query-path (pool 6) figures for any window that includes a --rule-outputs run: a tenant that never queries can turn from not measured into measured there. This run read pool 6 before counting, so its own pool-6 figures are unaffected

a share compares a point-in-time count with pool 1's window-average active series, so the two diverge whenever series are changing: a rule added or edited, or series repopulating after a restart or rollout. Read the share as indicative then, and re-run once the count has settled
